classification.difficultyReason: Model a familiar context with a binomial variable and combine exact probabilities for at least and fewer than events.

content.prompt:
The probability that dogs of a certain breed will have black spots is $\frac25$.

If a dog of this breed has 5 pups, find the probability that:

answer.worked:
Let $X$ count the pups with black spots. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,\frac25)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=3)&=\binom53\left(\frac25\right)^3\left(\frac35\right)^2\\&=\frac{144}{625}.\end{aligned}$$

Let $X$ count the pups with black spots. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,\frac25)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=0)&=\left(\frac35\right)^5\\&=\frac{243}{3125}.\end{aligned}$$

Let $X$ count the pups with black spots. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,\frac25)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=4)&=\binom54\left(\frac25\right)^4\left(\frac35\right)\\&=\frac{48}{625}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: at least 3 will have black spots

answer.worked:
Let $X$ count the pups with black spots. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,\frac25)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X\ge3)&=P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5)\\&=\frac{144}{625}+\frac{48}{625}+\left(\frac25\right)^5\\&=\frac{992}{3125}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: fewer than 3 will have black spots

answer.worked:
Let $X$ count the pups with black spots. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,\frac25)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X<3)&=1-P(X\ge3)\\&=1-\frac{992}{3125}\\&=\frac{2133}{3125}.\end{aligned}$$
